neighbours.label: Christ's atoning death on the cross (crucifixion/atonement theology: 'died on the cross ⟦for⟧ …', 'bore our sins ⟦on⟧ the tree', the lifted-up serpent), not Christian talk in general
fire: The apostle taught that Christ died on the cross for our sins.
The hymn says the Saviour bore our guilt upon the tree at Calvary.
As Moses raised the bronze serpent, so the Son of Man was lifted up.
Believers are saved by the blood that Jesus shed on the cross for sinners.
The sermon explained how the Lamb of God was sacrificed on the cross for the world.
Paul wrote that the Messiah was crucified to atone for the sins of many.
The creed confesses that the Lord suffered and died on a cross to redeem us.
Isaiah foretold a servant who would carry the iniquity of us all to his death.
quiet: The apostle taught that believers should pray every morning.
The hymn says the shepherd leads his flock beside still waters.
As Moses led the people out of Egypt, they sang by the sea.
Believers gather on Sunday to sing and share a meal.
The sermon explained how the early church chose its deacons.
Paul wrote that the churches should care for widows and orphans.
The creed confesses that God made heaven and earth.
Isaiah foretold a time when the desert would bloom.

notes: Card: 'lifted⟦ up⟧', bronze ' serpent', 'iniqu|ity of us all', 'bore their sins⟦ on⟧ the cross', 'A|ton|ement', 'die⟦ on⟧ a cross'; the + pole is general Christian vocabulary (teacher, prayer, deeds). Probes: 'bore our sins … on the tree' 0.76, lifted-up serpent 0.59, 'died on the cross for' 0.57; an Old Testament lamb sacrifice 0.15, a pastor preaching 0.00, 'hung on the wall' 0.00. Near misses stay Christian and drop the crucifixion.
